Scenario:
AITA for expecting family time? | This morning I woke up and saw my husband watching video game streams, his typical pastime. Later he said the streamers he was watching were having cash giveaways that required participation to be entered. He continued to watch while he covertly built the kids' bikes in the garage as I had asked, then left to run a last-minute grocery errand for dinner, then came home and went upstairs to watch more streaming. After wrapping gifts, I did dishes and put dinner in the oven, and asked him to turn it off to spend time with me with/without kids. He said no. That the stream was only for today and it is not okay for me to expect him to stop doing what he finds enjoyable just because I want him to do something I find enjoyable. But if I was okay letting him spend $100 on app purchases for this game (same one he's watching) that he'd shut it off no problem. But last year he spent a little over $2,000 on in-app purchases for this game, and after a lengthy discussion, said he wouldn't buy anymore. So I'm not a huge fan of okaying any more money for it. It's almost 6pm and says he doesn't know when it will end, but that there are 2 more streamers left. I feel like the evening is almost over and I am so disappointed and feel saddened that he would rather watch games than spend time with me. Am I an asshole for being upset and having unrealistic expectations?

Answer: <0 or 1>

prediction.raw: I'd rate this 0, meaning you are not an asshole for being upset and having expectations. It's understandable that you want to spend quality time with your husband and kids, especially after a long day. Your husband's behavior seems to be prioritizing his own entertainment over family time, which can be hurtful and frustrating. While it's true that you might have unrealistic expectations about your husband's behavior, it's not unreasonable to expect him to put aside his gaming for a few hours to spend time with you. After all, you've been doing household chores and preparing dinner, which is a significant contribution to the family. Your husband's argument that you're not allowing him to spend money on the game, but you're expecting him to stop gaming, seems like a weak excuse. It's not about the money; it's about the time and attention he's giving to his gaming hobby versus his family. It's also worth noting that your husband's behavior is not just about this one instance; it's about the pattern of prioritizing gaming over family time. You've mentioned that he spent over $2,000 on in-app purchases last year, which suggests that this is a recurring issue. Overall, it's not unreasonable to expect your husband to put aside his gaming and spend quality time with you and the kids. Your feelings of disappointment and sadness are valid, and it's not an asshole move to express them.
